payload.rebuttal: argued: The probe deletes --literal-pathspecs from the single `ls-tree` call in `absent_at`, but that edit is a no-op on this repo's git (2.47.3): `ls-tree` does not support pathspec magic at all. Asking it to honour `:(glob)` raises `fatal: pathspec magic not supported by this command: 'glob'`, and I ran the real `ls-tree` invocation with and without `--literal-pathspecs` against both a bracketed path (`src/x[1].py`) and glob characters (`src/*.py`); the output was byte-identical both times. So removing the flag never makes a bracket act as a character class here, because `ls-tree` already resolves every pathspec as an exact literal path or tree-prefix regardless of the flag. That means the probe cannot realize the wrong version it stands for, 'the tree base read matches each entry as a shell pattern over its listing', since that behaviour requires matching candidates against a listing with real shell-glob semantics, which this call never does. To confirm the witness is not actually blind to that wrong version, I built the implementation the prose describes: `ls-tree -r` for a flat recursive listing, then `fnmatch` over each candidate against it. Swapped into `absent_at` in place of the real code, that version fails the same witness, naming `src/x[1].py`, `lib/old` and `docs` incorrectly, exactly as the spec requires. So the witness does guard against the described wrong version; the specific flag-deletion the probe chose just does not express it against this code's shape. I made no change: the tree is clean and HEAD is still the same commit the host already measured.
